reason:
b-017 merged PR #395, but #239 is still open — and that is correct rather than a miss.

PR #395 is titled "feat(everyday): the stage says what it is drawing (#239 AC2)" and delivered **one of that issue's five acceptance criteria**: the stage's text equivalent. Verified on trunk, not inferred from the title — `packages/viz/src/everyday/stageScreen.ts` carries `STAGE_ANNOUNCE_MS` and calls `describeFrame`.

The other four acceptance criteria are untouched:
- an automated accessibility sweep running in CI
- every mode completable using the keyboard alone
- a colour-blind check on the eight shaft tints and the queue-age scale
- a screen-reader walkthrough, and its findings remediated

So neither branch the loop can choose between applies: the fix is on trunk and is right, and the issue is open because the batch was scoped to a fifth of it. **Do not close #239 on the strength of this PR.**

What a human decides: either keep #239 open and split the remaining four criteria into separately batchable issues, or close it and file the remainder. The four are heterogeneous — a CI job, a keyboard journey suite, a colour-encoding change and a manual walkthrough — so one issue is unlikely to be one batch.

Operationally: this escalation names #239, so `merged_leaving_open` will not raise it again, and triage skips it because it lists only issues it has not already recorded. Nothing will pick the remaining four criteria up without that human action. #239 is labelled P1.

b-037 merged PR #394, but #369 is still open — and that is correct rather than a miss.

PR #394 ("skip to the end, and the two ways it refuses") delivered the **skip control** half of a two-half issue. Verified on trunk, not inferred from the title: `packages/viz/src/everyday/stageScreen.ts:1066` defines `skipToEnd()`. The engineering half of the speed criterion is there too — `DEFAULT_STAGE_SIM_PER_REAL_S` is a single constant in `everyday/stageScreenModel.ts:248`, consulted by Settings' *Default speed* row and by `profile.ts`, which is exactly the "read from one place, not two" the criterion asks for. AC5's corpus seeding is also done: `honesty/surfaces.ts:171` imports `STAGE_SPEEDS`.

**AC1 is not met, and the reason it is not is not an engineering gap.** The shipped constant is `30`, i.e. `30×` — neither of the two candidates. The criterion requires the opening speed to be `1×` or `4×`, *"the choice recorded with the playtest that made it"*, and § D525 says in terms that which watching rung opens a run is a playtest's to decide, not the build's. AC6 (re-checking `docs/28` § 6's four motion rules against the chosen default) is blocked behind it for the same reason.

So neither branch the loop can choose between applies: the fix is on trunk and is right, and the issue is open on a criterion no autonomous pass may settle. **Do not close #369, and do not let a later batch pick a default to close it** — a value chosen by a builder rather than a playtest would satisfy the checkbox and violate the decision behind it.

What a human decides: run the playtest and record the choice on #369, or split AC1 and AC6 into a playtest-blocked issue and close the rest.

Note on the pattern, since this is the second `merged_leaving_open` escalation in one pass (the other is #239). The module's usual diagnosis is that `land` step 6 is being skipped. That is **not** what happened here: in both cases the PR deliberately carried a subset marker in its title (`#239 AC2`, and this one's two-half scope) and left the issue open on purpose. The upstream cause is batching accepting a multi-criterion issue as one batch, not landing failing to close. Worth fixing there rather than in `land`.

b-050 merged PR #397, but #238 is still open — and that is correct rather than a miss. The PR title says so itself: *"enforce charter S9's bundle budget, **and only that one** (#238 B2)"*.

Verified on trunk rather than inferred from the title. `packages/viz/src/everyday/builtBundle.browser.test.ts` enforces **B2**, the gzipped bundle budget, and its own docstring states the scope:

> These cases are **B2 and only B2**, and saying which is not a hedge … So **`charter S9` stays partially instrumented**, and this file does not let the verdict read otherwise: `docs/22` § 6 forbids meeting a criterion by weakening it.

Nothing on trunk defines a cold-load, frame-time or main-thread-blocking budget — searched across `packages/viz/` and `.github/`, no hits.

Against #238's four acceptance criteria: budgets are defined for **one** of the four quantities; CI fails on that one; the three main-thread simulation surfaces are neither moved to a worker nor bounded; and S9 is instrumented in part, which the code says plainly.

**The remaining two budgets are blocked on something an autonomous pass cannot supply**, which is the part worth a human's attention:

- **B1** (time to interactive ≤ 3 000 ms) needs run history this repository does not keep — `docs/31` § 3 requires it to gate on a rolling comparison, never a single run, because *"a single-run wall clock on a shared VM is a coin flip"*.
- **B3** (main-thread block ≤ 800 ms) needs a CPU-throttle factor calibrated against a real mid-range laptop, with the calibration recorded with its date and machine. There is no such machine here, and **issue #335 is the live record of what this gate does without one**: `BLOCKED_FRAME_GAP_MS` red at 404.9 ms on a runner against 41 ms and 39 ms on one host, and it reproduced at **10 433 ms** while #397 was being written.

So: **do not close #238**, and do not let a later batch close it by adding a wall-clock gate — #335 is the standing evidence that such a gate measures the runner, not the product, and `docs/22` § 6 forbids meeting a criterion by weakening it.

What a human decides: supply the calibration machine and the run-history store (unblocking B1 and B3), or split #238 so that B2 is closed and B1/B3/AC3 become a separate issue blocked on #335.

Pattern note: this is the **third** `merged_leaving_open` escalation in this pass (#239, #369, #238), and all three are the same shape — a multi-criterion issue batched as one, whose PR honestly carried a subset marker in its title and left the issue open on purpose. The module's usual diagnosis is that `land` step 6 is being skipped; that is not what is happening. The upstream fix belongs in batching, which should not accept a multi-criterion issue as a single batch.

reason:
**Both gates are clear and this batch stops here for a human — by policy, not by failure.**

`data/wrinkles.json` matches `protected_paths` (`data/**`) in `.foreman/config.json`, so `land.py blockers` refuses the merge however green it is, and the product owner's standing ruling for `data/` is draft-and-approve. This PR is the draft.

**State**
- CI: `full_green` on `4b2c8c1` — 15 checks on that exact commit, nothing stale. Green on all five pushes, including the `browser` leg, which cannot be run locally.
- Review: **clean** at round 5, with a revert check measured against the right base (`failed_as_expected`, reverting the complete-case guard turns the R1 case red).
- Local gate: full suite green in every project (9 862 passed), `tsc -b` clean, `scripts/review-gates.mjs` clean.

**What is being approved.** `data/wrinkles.json` is 25 authored templates — 38 concrete wrinkles once the parameter axes are multiplied out. The figures are **drafted game feel, not measurements**, and the file's own `$comment` says so, in the same register as `data/price-schedule.json`. Every effect is expressed only in the four fields the engine actually reads, which `wrinkles/parse.ts` enforces at load, and `shift/events.test.ts` sweeps all 25 through a real simulation asserting each one changes the run in the direction it claims.

**Three of § 17's six named wrinkle kinds are deliberately absent** — doors slowed on one car, a sky lobby closed, a floor's occupancy spiked. None can be expressed in `EventEffect`'s four fields, so they are recorded in the library's `unexpressible` list with the seam each one needs rather than authored as captions no passenger would experience. The parser refuses an emptied list.

**Two things the owner may want to weigh before approving:**

1. **Day 1 draws `ordinary`.** The draw indexes on `day - 1` specifically so a new player's first day carries no wrinkle, which is § 20.13 (*"saturation is something the player causes by week two, never the state a level ships in"*). Indexing on `day` had put a car out of service on day 1.
2. **§ 17's gate keeps 8 of 38 candidate days and discards 24, with 6 it refuses to judge** at Garden Apartments. That is a measurement of the drafted content, not a verdict on it — the gate is an offline instrument with no shipped caller, and nothing in the tree claims the shipped library passed it. If the intent is that every shipped wrinkle should earn its place, that is a content decision and a follow-up.

findings.summary: § 20.3's closing arithmetic is wrong. '±0.22 ... wider than the distance between any two of the charter's four targets' is false: the only two commensurable targets are charter S2 (60 %) and charter S4 (25 %), 0.35 apart, which is wider than 0.22, not narrower.

After that deletion docs/26 still tells a reader, in four places, that the deleted content is there: § 19 line 1746 ('the grounds it rests on and the exposure a floor cannot close are all declared in § 20.3'), § 11 line 1036 ('which states the figure and the grounds it rests on'), § 20.2's P5 refusal cell line 1782 (which refuses '**and § 20.3's complement rule**', now a dangling reference inside the very table the gate parses), and § 20.7 item 1 line 1960 ('§ 20.3 ground 2 — the fixed window is what the floor rests on'). § 19 is the checklist handed to a legal reviewer. Restore an assertion that § 20.3 carries the grounds it is cited for, and pin P5's cited 'complement rule' and § 20.7's cited 'ground 2' the same both-directions way case 7 already pins § 20.6's claim against § 11.

findings.summary: § 19 has not stopped restating. 'the floor, the grounds it rests on and the exposure a floor cannot close are all declared in § 20.3' is still a substantive characterisation of § 20.3, it is unpinned, and round 4's exact escape route reproduces: inverting it leaves all nine cases green. The same sentence claims these things 'are deliberately not restated here' while restating one of them, and § 11 line 1036 has the same shape.
findings.failure_scenario: Rewriting the clause to '**the floor, the grounds it rests on and the fact that a floor closes every exposure are all declared in § 20.3**' — a direct inversion of the claim — runs `Tests 9 passed (9)`. That is the identical mutation round 4 raised as a finding, reported as fixed and still passing. The test's own comment at line 333 asserts the opposite: 'There is then nothing at those sites for a later edit to make false.' It is false as written. Combined with the first finding: a later edit that moves the complement rule out of § 20.3 into a new § 20.8 leaves the legal reviewer's checklist telling a lawyer that § 20.3 declares an exposure a floor cannot close, when it does not, with the gate green. Either drop the characterisation and leave only the pointer ('it is declared in § 20.3, and deliberately not restated here'), or pin it.

findings.summary: The per-site 'no people-count' guard is digit-only (`/\d+ people/`), so a referring site restating the floor as a spelled-out word passes. docs/26 spells numbers out routinely — 'eight people are in a room' (§ 20.5), 'Two people on one browser profile' (§ 3), 'the ten people it' (§ 9).
findings.failure_scenario: Editing § 5.4 to read 'A row under the floor of twenty people is refused rather than published' runs `Tests 9 passed (9)`. The same edit written as 'the floor of 20 people' is correctly caught. So the original defect — the figure restated at § 5.4 and going stale when § 20.3 moves — is still reachable through the phrasing the document itself prefers for small integers.

findings.summary: Round 4's spurious-match low is not gone; it moved. The document-wide sweep is now correctly anchored to 'minimum cell size is N people', but the two per-site guards are still unanchored (`/\d+ people/` and `/(?:zero|...|six|\d+) (?:stated )?grounds/`) and are now must-not-match assertions over § 5.4, § 11 and § 19 in their entirety. § 11 is the engineering-debt register and § 19 is a nineteen-row legal checklist expected to grow; both have legitimate reason to state a count.
findings.failure_scenario: Adding an unrelated § 11 register row '#205 recruits 12 people and whether that is enough is not settled here' fails with `§ 11 restates a people-count. Point at § 20.3 instead`. Adding an unrelated § 19 checklist row 'Option C refuses on two grounds and neither is settled' fails with `§ 19 restates how many grounds § 20.3 gives`. Both are false reds naming the wrong cause, and both are the kind of row those two sections exist to accumulate. Scope the guards to the cell-size sentence rather than to the whole section.

findings.summary: Stale test name and stale PR claim. The case is still titled 'declares the minimum aggregate cell size as a number with its unit, and § 5.4 agrees', but this round removed every assertion touching § 5.4 from its body — it now checks only that § 20.3 declares a floor greater than 1. The PR description still lists '§ 5.4 and § 20.3 disagreeing about the floor — red' as a property of the gate.
findings.failure_scenario: No agreement between § 5.4 and § 20.3 is checked anywhere, and by design there is nothing to agree about since § 5.4 no longer carries a figure. A maintainer reading the case name or the PR body believes a cross-section agreement check exists and will not add one. In a repository whose standing rule is that a refusal or a claim must be pinned by a run rather than by another sentence, a test titled for an assertion it does not make is the same defect one layer up. (The case also leaves a stray blank line where the deleted block was.)
